evals.prompt: Review two invitation tests. src/hooks/useInviteForm.test.tsx renders useInviteForm in isolation, mocks the API client, and asserts internal setter calls. src/components/InviteForm.spec.tsx isolates the form and only asserts that an onSubmit spy was called. evals.expected_output: A structured review that evaluates the isolated tests against the user-visible regression and recommends integration coverage of the form's submission behavior using the existing ValidInvite story.
assertions: The report follows the required section order. In Findings by Test, each assessed test has one top-level bullet starting with its backticked path and exactly one backticked allowed status on the same line.

Findings cite the supplied production and test paths. Framework-bound claims, if any, have official documentation and source permalinks.

evals.prompt: Assess checkout as a critical journey. tests/unit/useCheckout.test.ts mocks auth, storage, the router, and the payment API and asserts internal step numbers. tests/checkout.spec.ts uses a real browser through Playwright, stubs every API response, starts at /checkout/payment, and verifies that the checkout route renders payment fields using the fetched cart. Production paths are src/checkout/useCheckout.ts and src/checkout/CheckoutPage.tsx. When the real authentication service issued its session and redirected the browser, the cart was lost and the return URL reopened an empty checkout. Restore a minimal safety net for this regression and assess both existing tests.
evals.expected_output: A review that distinguishes the current frontend integration check from the proposed system-level coverage and explains the concrete seams that the proposed checkout test must exercise.
assertions: The current Playwright scenario is recognized as frontend integration coverage with stubbed responses and direct entry.

The critical regression is covered by an E2E scenario that exercises the real authentication and session boundary, cart persistence, browser redirect and return navigation, and the restored cart as the user-visible outcome.
Each existing test receives one allowed status. Before a move or removal, the recommendation accounts for currently protected behaviors the proposed E2E would leave uncovered.

evals.prompt: Should we keep tests/unit/orderStatus.test.ts? It passes arbitrary strings into renderOrderStatus and expects unknown values to render 'Unknown'. The production type in src/orders/orderStatus.ts is `type OrderStatus = 'pending' | 'paid' | 'cancelled'`, and internal callers are typed. The product contract requires rejection of unsupported API values in src/orders/decodeOrder.ts before they reach the renderer. The production decoder currently trusts the response. Assess the test and propose a minimal replacement for the missing guarantee.
evals.expected_output: An assessment that distinguishes the compile-time guarantee for typed callers from runtime validation of the API payload, and proposes a check that detects the actual boundary failure.
assertions: The review retains the compile-time guarantee of the closed union for typed internal callers and recognizes the untrusted payload as a separate runtime risk.
The proposed check exercises the production decoding boundary and verifies rejection of unsupported values before rendering. Its scope is justified by what it validates.

Findings by Test has one top-level bullet starting with the backticked path tests/unit/orderStatus.test.ts and one backticked allowed status on the same line. The finding cites src/orders/orderStatus.ts and ties the missing runtime coverage to src/orders/decodeOrder.ts.
